children: The French year-ahead baseload electricity contract hit its highest level since December 2023 at €90.65 ($105.39) per megawatt hour on Thursday, tracking higher gas prices.
The French wholesale front-year contract, the country's benchmark electricity contract, has risen continuously over the last 10 days as it tracks spiralling gas costs.

France relies on its 57-reactor nuclear fleet for about 70% of its electricity production, but European markets are interconnected so high gas costs, which set the price of electricity in Europe, can drive French costs higher.

The strong gas price and reduced nuclear availability have also driven spot electricity prices to winter levels in recent months, as Europe grappled with heatwaves that took nuclear reactors offline and reduced already low hydropower stocks.
Labour strikes are also threatening French nuclear output next week, while a heavy maintenance schedule is expected to cut supply in the fourth quarter of 2026.

The fourth quarter power balance looks particularly exposed given heavy French nuclear works, which will cut exports to Germany requiring gas to meet much of the shortfall with little additional coal generation available, analysts at Energy Aspects said in a weekly update.

A heavier stockdraw in the fourth quarter would leave Europe entering 2027 with lower inventories than currently forecast, tightening storage deliverability and forcing Europe to bid higher for liquefied natural gas, the analysts said.
